title: ✨Have you heard of the #MyDigitalCloset challenge?
content:
We’re currently running a really cool challenge, and the experience has been so fun and special!

The theme of the challenge,**#MyDigitalCloset** , invites participants to combine their items with CONNECT’s motion to tell unique stories in their own digital spaces.

So far, this challenge has had two rounds, and the submissions we’ve received have been truly moving. From stunning outfits to creative concepts, the entries are brimming with passion, energy, and originality.

* * *

We’re excited to share the highlight videos from Round 1 and Round 2 with you.

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NibhrPO2PnY

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e5cmrTtVkH8

These videos are being shared through our Instagram([@closet_connect_official](https://www.instagram.com/closet_connect_official/)) and community channels, and they’ve also received great feedback and brought a lot of joy within CLO.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5266c10158e14383825d34f1c4e49346/images/34c12928acfb45af8fb7ca31e7b2ba41challenge.png)

Even if your work didn’t make it into the highlight video, your participation was an important part of what made this challenge so special.

* * *

# **_Did you miss out on the first two rounds? Don’t worry!_**

**The 3rd challenge is coming soon, and it’s going to be even more exciting and thrilling—so stay tuned!**

We sincerely thank everyone who took part in **#MyDigitalCloset** challenge, and every moment we shared through it was truly precious. Don’t worry if you missed out this time; there will be plenty more opportunities coming your way. We look forward to seeing even more creative challenges ahead!

Plus, if you have any challenge ideas you’d love to see, feel free to share them in the comments!

**_Let’s enjoy this challenge together!🎉🎀_**

  


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/5266c10158e14383825d34f1c4e49346/images/f647f4f6604d47478168a602756ef5db%EC%8B%9C%ED%80%80%EC%8A%A4%2002_reel.00_00_02_20.%EC%8A%A4%ED%8B%B8%20001.png)

title: Export CLO3D Avatar Animation with Textures to Blender 4.0
content:
Hi there CLO Team,

I noticed there have been a few threads where people are asking how to export a CLO3D Avatar with a native CLO3D Animation including textures, and import the CLO3D Avatar with Animation and Textures into Blender.

Also, here a CLO team member mentioned:

> _-You can export an Alembic(OGAWA) to have the animation of the avatar + garment. Textures will be missing and you have to add them later in the 3rd party software._
> 
> _-You can export a gLTF 2.0 (GLTF) to have the garment animation + textures.  
>   
> _[_https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/4407342113945/comments/4407493415577_](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/4407342113945/comments/4407493415577)

I have tried to export a CLO3D Avatar with an applied Animation (via .mtn applied) as OGAWA (.alembic) file multiple times, but when importing the .abc file into Blender, unfortunately the exported 3D object doesn't come with unwrapped UV's and materials at all, so unwrapping becomes a very hard and tedious task if one wants to reuse the original textures. Please correct me if I am missing something.

Therefore I was wondering if you have a tutorial video or advice on best practice how to solve this part "Textures will be missing and you have to add them later in the 3rd party software."?

The alternative workflow that works for me would be to use an external animation via Mixamo as I've explained in this quick tutorial here:

<https://www.instagram.com/p/DCrPyLGO7qC/>

I have an existing garment simulation with a native CLO3D Avatar Animation which I would like to keep, therefore I am asking before having to redo the process with the alternative workflow, going via Mixamo.

Many thanks in advance and I'm looking forward to your feedback!

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: I just doing some test on the avatar output, not sure if this is what you looking for: You can just output the avatar and the garment with the fbx format( remember to choose single object when you doing the output. that is still separately. ) so when you get into Blender. You will have a avatar with the armature you can edit also same texture mapping as when you see in CLO. But for the garment animation you need a extra Alembic or a mdd to transfer the date to the garment in Blender. But there have an issue. i still looking for the reason why. When you output in this way, the avatar will have some motion delay or not matching in between the steps. But you can still edit the armature for those motion.

Comment 2: Hi Melody, thank you for looking into this so quickly! I just tried exporting the CLO3D avatar (Luka) with a native CLO3D animation as USD and imported it into Blender and it indeed works including textures! :)Only challenge that I am facing with this option is that the hair texture doesn't work correctly. I tried changing the "Viewport Display" settings in the Material Settings to "Blend Mode" = "Opaque / Alpha Clip / Alpha Hashed / Alpha Blend", as well as the "Shadow Mode" = "None / Alpha Clip / Alpha Hashed"If your colleagues might have a hint on how to fix this, that would be amazing. Thanks again!
Reply 1: Hi there, unfortunately, we don't know a fix for what you're describing, I think you must inquire on a Blender forum, sorry!
Reply 2: Hi Melody, thanks a lot for your feedback! I also wanted to let you know that by coincidence hair textures (including all body textures) work fine, when CLO avatars are being animated with Mixamo and then imported into Blender as FBX animation. Maybe your developers can get a hint on how to set up the USD file to get hair textures working correctly in 3D programs, when importing them.If you need some example images for any of the described issues, please don't hesitate to let me know!

Comment 3: Hi, unfortunately the UV Editor cannot bake the maps of avatars, only of garments. If you are working with an Alembic file, you have to bake the UVs separately and relink them in Blender manually. For the problem of the UVs of the avatar, our colleagues just tried out that USD exports with both animation and UV maps. Have you tried exporting everything together in a USD file?
content_description: This page provides guidance and best practices for exporting CLO3D avatars with animations and textures for seamless import into Blender.

title: What's on my desk? #whatsonmydesk
content:
While I'm updating my GPU driver (you should do that too! 😉), I decided to join the challenge and share #whatsonmydesk as a CLO designer.  


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/2ea97ae4f05945a09248d732a70b1a2f/images/4e15064637f14369b987be35faec2883WhatsApp%20Image%202025-01-16%20at%208.51.34%20AM.jpeg)

When I'm working in the office, I love using my two additional screens while keeping my notebook screen turned off—only using it for the webcam. 💻✨

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/2ea97ae4f05945a09248d732a70b1a2f/images/9dc16d7fcf6c47b3b26fb8fa8d382da3WhatsApp%20Image%202025-01-16%20at%208.51.35%20AM.jpeg)

As you can see, I have a lot of toys and CLO merchandise that truly represent me. You'll spot my Capybara pencil (fun fact: I'm from Curitiba, Brazil, a city known for its many capybaras! 😂). You can also see some 3D-printed figurines that I hand-painted, and of course, Harry, a thoughtful gift from a friend.  
  


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202501/2ea97ae4f05945a09248d732a70b1a2f/images/f5886e0d4fee4b1ba295f1db4c06bff9WhatsApp%20Image%202025-01-16%20at%208.51.34%20AM%20%281%29.jpeg)

Next up is Ryan the lion and another Pop Mart figurine I collected during my visit to the Shanghai office. Lastly, but certainly not least, a must-have item on my desk: the measuring tape! 📏

title: 📢Community Event: "What's on my desk?"
content:
## _Hello everyone!_

## _We are excited to announce our first community event:_

## **_"What's on my desk?" 🎉_**

This event is all about sharing the unique and creative setups of your workspaces. Whether it's your home office, studio, or any place where you get things done, we want to see it!  


* * *

# **How to participate:**

  1. Take a photo of your desk or workspace.

  2. Share it in **@General board as a post.**

  3. Add a brief description of your setup and any interesting items you have on your desk

  4. **Don't forget to add the tag "whatsonmydesk"!**




* * *

We can't wait to see your amazing workspaces! Let's connect with fellow community members and see how they work. 🖥️✨

** _Happy sharing!_**

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Wait, I need to clean up my desk first... 😵

Comment 2: It’s really exciting news! 🏄 If creative workspaces are shared, it will surely lead to a wealth of ideas and collaboration, inspiring even more remarkable outcomes. 👖 Does the workspace... or desk need to be specifically related to fashion, or can it be open to other fields as well?
Reply 1: Hi! It doesn't have to be related to fashion! Feel free to share anything on your desk that you want to share!💫
content_description: A page to invite community members to share photos and descriptions of their unique workspaces for the "What's on my desk?" event.
